headline_stat.name: block prior decodable from 400ms pre-stimulus activity

stated_limitation: The effect was not uniform across sessions, consistent with genuine biological and recording variability rather than an artificially clean result.

justification.dataset: 000149 is the canonical IBL block-prior choice-world dataset and the paradigm (0%-contrast trials in extreme blocks) is exactly the standard way to isolate an internally generated decision bias.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via LINDI, good units selected by label==1.0 with bulk spike-time reads, counts aligned to a 400 ms window verified to fall within the enforced pre-stimulus quiescence (min gap 0.443 s).
justification.analysis: Cross-validated logistic regression with a label-permutation null (which correctly handles the class imbalance) is appropriate, but there is no multiple-comparison correction across the 8 tests and the choice-vs-block confound in the choice decoder is not addressed.
justification.correctness: Every reported p-value and accuracy reproduces exactly from the committed notebook output, is internally consistent with the figures, and rests on sound permutation statistics with no physically impossible values.
justification.figures: Decoding figures (fig3/4) show observed accuracy against permutation nulls clearly with p-values, but fig5's example unit is the max-|t| unit hand-picked from the one session whose population did not decode, a flattering supplementary example.
justification.honesty: The write-up reports 3/4 and 2/4 sessions, names the non-significant session explicitly, gives borderline p-values at face value, and states plainly the effect is not uniform, so no claim exceeds the evidence.
justification.verdict: Core work is sound and believable, but I would ask for multiple-comparison correction, discussion of the choice-block confound, and a more representative example unit before fully accepting.
